utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't want to interrupt the answer of the witness but I do object -- I don't object when Ms. Korner is asking the witness about the Law on Interior because being a chief of the CSB it is understandable that he is aware of the law and the provisions of the law. Also, I didn't object when she was asking him about the laws on All People's Defence because, as we heard from the witness, he worked in the national defence office in Derventa before he became the chief of the CSB. But now I must object that what is elicited from the witness are provisions of the law and comments on the law which have nothing to do whatsoever with his professional and his knowledge. I must say that I'm also astonished by the fact that none of the questions which Ms. Korner posed today were not put to the expert witness when he was on the stand over here. Not a single one, not a comments on any of these laws have ever been put by the Office of the Prosecutor to the police expert which we brought as a previous witness. And I'm not entirely sure what is the -- what is the -- the case of the Prosecution anymore because --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think this is going into -- I think -- I think this is now going into a discussion of evidence and policy, and I don't think it's proper that the witness should listen to this. I've got a perfectly good reason which I will explain for why I'm asking these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, it's nearly time for the break, so perhaps the witness can be excused. The usher could escort the witness out a little ahead of the usual time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, if I may then finish before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: In terms of the second limb, Mr. Zecevic, of your objection or observation, wouldn't the -- well, my impression, and I confess I may be wrong, is that the line of question that Ms. Korner was pursuing is in terms of what the law is. She is taking advantage of having the CSB chief on the stand who is working with this and applying it on a day-to-day basis. So whether she pursued the interpretation with the police expert is neither here nor there, but in terms of the first part of your objection, do I understand it to be that the questions that are being asked are outside of the -- are questions on the interpretation of the law which are straying outside of the ordinary work or expertise of this witness? Is that what I understand your objection to be?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Precisely so, Your Honours. What I tried to explain is the fact that I was not objecting to any comments on the laws which have something to do with his profession or his duties as a chief of the CSB. But then what is happening is that Ms. Korner is putting to the witness her understanding of the law for a comment, and that particular part deals with the laws that have nothing to do with his either profession or his -- or his education, if I may say so. Thank you. That was the point of my objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I may have phrased it rather badly, but, in fact, I was asking for his understanding, not what the law was about Crisis Staffs and whatever, but his understanding on the position he was in during this period of the ability of Crisis Staffs who had taken over from Municipal Assemblies. As regards to the first part, this man is, in the Prosecution's submission, and this is something we will be saying at the end of the case, much more of an expert on these matters than the expert -- the so-called expert that was actually called. And in any event what questions were put to Mr. Bajagic is, as Your Honours have pointed out, entirely irrelevant. But, Your Honours, what I was asking for was his understanding of the powers of the Crisis Staff if they devolved from the Municipal Assembly, which I didn't think was a matter of dispute at all because we've called a lot of evidence about it which has not been challenged including an expert on Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, your last remark calls for a reference back to what the presiding judge raised this morning, namely that given the constraints on time, I just wondered whether this is the best possible use of the time that we have with this witness to take him through his understanding of the situation in respect of the Crisis Staffs which are matters that, as you say, are neither contested nor uncovered by the evidence that we already have. So is this really beneficial to your case?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't know whether Your Honours have read through Mr. Stanisic's interview, which I did in preparation for this witness. It's my understanding is that the Defence propose to try and rely on what he said in interview. I'm, therefore, dealing with this witness with some of the assertions that he made in interview and that's why otherwise I would not, may I say, be spending time on the Law of Internal Affairs and the questions such as the questions that I've been asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we will take the adjournment now and continue with this in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, I just want to deal with a couple of more articles on the Law on Internal Affairs and then we'll move into other matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, I suppose I better have it back up again. It's P530. And Article 33, which is on the fourth page of the English and I think the same in B/C/S. If we can highlight the B/C/S for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That deals with the tasks and activities of the ministry at its seat, and in particular as it affected you, monitors directs and co-ordinates the activity of the Security Services Centre. Now, that, I think, was identical under the old Socialist Republic of BiH law; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In essence, yes, I don't have the other text to compare it with this one but I believe that's the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we then just deal, please, with Article 43, which I think encapsulates what you've already told us, which you will find on the sixth page, yeah, page 6 of the English and the same in B/C/S: "Authorised officials must execute orders issued by the minister or by their immediate senior official for the purpose of performing activities and tasks related to national and public security, except when such orders contravene the constitution and the law." Mr. Bjelosevic, effectively that's what you've already told us, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the final article I want to move on to, the events --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Article 126, please, which is on page 13, I think. 126. Of the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Not in the English, I am afraid.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have it there?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We'll have to go to the next page: "The centres for public security centres and public security stations the Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the territory of the Republic of the Serbian people shall be closed on the day that this law enters into force and shall resume their work as organising units of the Ministry of the Interior of the Serbian Republic ..." Now, that's what Mr. Mandic's telegram was saying, wasn't it, and that's what the Law of Internal Affairs was saying?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And as you've already told us and I don't want to go back over it, you decided, in effect, that you weren't, from what you tell us -- you weren't going to comply with that? You have to say yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we discussed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Now, I want very, very briefly, please, to deal a little bit with the events that you have described at length to Mr. Zecevic of Bosanski Brod and Slavonski Brod and to a certain extent Derventa because, as we said -- as you heard me say at the time, this is not a matter that's part of our indictment. Could you have a look, please, at a document which has got the number 20032, tab 88. It's not tab 88 in the Defence bundle. You have to look at it on the screen, I am afraid.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, can we go to the next page, please, in B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This was an article that was published in "Slobodna Bosnia" on the 24th of May, 2001, and it deals with the activities on a trial that had taken place in respect of Taifun.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I want you to look, please, at the B/C/S, I think it's the next page, and in English it's the third page. In English, please, the page after that. Fourth page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I just want to confirm either with you, Mr. Bjelosevic, or any of the Defence counsel that we are looking -- you are able to see something headed, "Explosions, Destruction, Incidents"? That is right, is it? Okay. Thank you. So it is. Do you see that heading, "Explosions, Destruction, Incidents."

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the only thing I can make out, in fact. The rest is very small print. Can it be enlarged, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. This is describing what is alleged to be one of the first operations of Taifun led by Branko Ratic, still a JNA officer -- was to destroy the bridge near Bosanski Brod in the autumn of 1991. The bridge was shelled from Mahala village on the Bosnian side. Three shells hit the bridge and an tanker truck on it and five shells fell on the centre of Slavonski Brod. Ratic was given logistical support by the then chief of the Doboj secure services centre, Mr. Bjelosevic, Andrija Bjelosevic. First question is: Is that right that there was a shelling? There was a destruction of the bridge in autumn of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at all. The bridge was blown up only sometime in 1992 but there was an incident of sorts at the time and an on-site investigation was carried out. I went to Brod to attend the scene personally, but the bridge wasn't destroyed. Later on, the administration got involved in the matter, the administration from the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina. They took charge of the investigation into who opened fire on from where. They took me, what I -- they took me to the place where the mortars were opening fire from, whereas from what I read here it's a bit preposterous. And we went to examine the place. However, had mortars opened fire from that particular spot, then the window panes on the house nearby would have been shattered. Furthermore, the tanker truck, I don't know what happened with it, but had it been full of gas, it would have been blown apart. So there were quite a few unknowns in my mind around this event, but there was an incident, that's true. As for the press coverage, that was very tendencious. I was even accused of causing the death of the chief of the public security sector in Doboj. Senad --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the last name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And Jasmin Halilovic, who was the head of the economic crime department, they perished in a traffic accident near Kakanj, and I had the long grown accustomed to such press coverage and tried to be impervious to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Is your answer, Yes there was some incident when the bridge was shelled, but you don't accept -- let's take that first part of the question. There was an incidents in autumn of 1991 when the bridge was shelled?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was some sort of fire there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You do not accept that it was done by Mr. Ratic who was then a JNA officer?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if it was he who did it. I don't know who caused it and what the motives were, but there was an incident. There was various circumstantial evidence at the time as to who was behind it. If you want to talk about the various versions, we can do that. What we read here is one of the versions but there are others, and I really don't know what is the truth of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you give logistical support to Mr. Ratic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's absurd. What sort of logistical support would it have been?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Why didn't you mention this incident when you gave your evidence about what was the events of Bosanski Brod and Slavonski Brod?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me when I say that I don't know. This was an incident that engendered several versions. One of the versions is that the Croatian forces staged the whole thing in order to close off the bridge. The second version was that it was this JNA officer who was behind it. I really don't know what the truthful version is. However, what followed next as of 15th of September were serious events, and I'm speaking about 15th of September, 1991. Since it was the administration that got involved in the case, they simply took the matter from our hands. As far as I remember, we had never received an official version of the events.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This happened, didn't it, long before the events that you've described which you say were the Croats attacking from a division between Slavonski and Bosanski Brod, or a division the other way around?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That wasn't long before. The first armed incident where shells were landing in the Slavonian part dated back to the 15th of September, whereas this was early September. I think that those events happened before the event we are just discussing now. As for my earlier testimony when I was being examined by the Defence, I didn't even mention the Slavonski Brod incident in the neighbourhood of Bjelis and it somehow cropped up yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. That's all I want to ask you about that. The only other matter I want to put to you, again it's only, I suggest, that you didn't mention when you gave your evidence, it's right, isn't it, that in Bosanski Brod the Serbs proclaimed yet another Serbian municipality in late February, early March?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the date, really. However, in early March there were armed clashes taking place. When the Serbian Brod municipality was declared, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: During the direct examination I hope you will remember that Ms. Korner was complaining and objecting to my line of questions concerning these municipalities, Derventa, Bosanski Brod and the like, saying that it is not in the indictment. And, therefore, on the suggestion of the Trial Chamber, I shortened the presentation of that particular part -- portion of my presentation in chief because it was the objection from the Office of the Prosecutor which to a certain extent the Trial Chamber accepted. Now, the witness -- it is put to the witness that he failed to mention these incidents in his direct examination, testing his credibility when, in fact, I didn't have the opportunity to ask the witness about this because there was an objection. I don't think that this is appropriate. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, of course, if Mr. Zecevic tells me that he had every intention of asking him about the first incident that we've seen in this article and the fact that a Serbian municipality was declared, then of course I would immediately withdraw any suggestion I had that he deliberately didn't mention it. So if Mr. Zecevic says he would have asked that had he been given further time, then I certainly won't make that suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: But, Ms. Korner, I'm not sure where this is going because my recollection of the point in examination-in-chief to which Mr. Zecevic refers is that upon the Prosecution's -- well, first of all, basically, it is always of doubtful assistance to ask the witness why didn't he volunteer something in as much as the procedure is usually one of a witness only answers a question that's asked. But coming back to the objection, my recollection is, and please correct me if I'm wrong -- is that the -- upon the Prosecution's objection to these municipalities who are not in the indictment, the witness's explanation was that the -- well, the explanation was that this arose because there was an overlap between the municipalities mentioned in the indictment and his areas of responsibility, and for that limited purpose, based on the objection, the basic objection of relevance, the limited questions were asked. So like Mr. Zecevic, I confess, I wonder why you are going down this road.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think the witness better leave court, Your Honour. I may say I'm somewhat surprised at Your Honour's remarks just now. I think I better explain because it's not in the way that Your Honour has expressed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness from the court.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours will recall that Mr. Zecevic was asking questions specifically about the events of Bosanski and Slavonski Brod, and when I first raised my objection and said I did not see the relevance of this, and I let it go on for some time and I can turn up, I can get Mr. Demirdjian to turn up the relevant pages, Mr. Zecevic explained, Your Honours accepted it and we went on. And I raised the objection a second time because, in particular, you will recall he gave a very, very long answer which bore no relationship to the question that actually Mr. Zecevic asked and went over again the Serb version of events in Bosanski Brod and Slavonski Brod. At the end I said that I was being put in a very difficult position because I didn't consider it relevant, and otherwise I would have to cross-examine on it. Your Honours left court at that stage saying they didn't -- you didn't consider it relevant and I didn't have to cross-examine or Judge Hall said that, and I'm paraphrasing. However, the next morning you came back and said, No, it was a matter for me. Now, Your Honours, I don't expect to -- this is literally the only two questions that I'm going to deal with because I do consider it's relevant and that is he we are going to be addressing you. But he was allowed to give his evidence, Mr. Zecevic was allowed to ask the questions on this basis, and, therefore, I'm in entitled to cross-examine, to point out that when Mr. Zecevic was going through it with him and asking the questions about this, that not once did he mention this incident, whether or not he was involved where the bridge was attacked before the events he described, nor did he mention at any stage, and he was the one coming out with most of the evidence -- that we would suggest part of the problem was caused by the fact that they had declared a Serbian municipality in Bosanski Brod. Those go directly to -- those are matters that go directly to the relevance or not of this evidence -- his own credibility. But as I say, if Mr. Zecevic asserts and of course I accept his word for this, that he would have asked about that early incidents, that he would have asked about the creation of the Serbian municipality, then I withdraw any suggestion that he deliberately avoided telling us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I hear what you've just said which is -- the only slight difficulty I have with that, though, is that in terms of the evidence which I appreciate you leading in terms of the testing the witness's credibility, but the -- I don't know that anything that counsel for Stanisic says whether what he would have done and therefore your withdrawing the question becomes evidence on which we can act. I'm a bit uncomfortable. I see you being permitted to explore the area to the limited extent that it came into the body of evidence in terms of testing the witness's credibility. But the last part of your terms of Mr. -- any representation Mr. Zecevic would give, I don't know that we can necessarily accept it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think this goes back perhaps very much to domestic practice, Your Honour. But quite often, you will hear people saying, You've never said that before, have you, and that will get counsel for either side, usually the Defence, and say, In actual fact it was in my instructions but I didn't consider it relevant, so that's why I didn't put it. So the suggestion that you make that someone has literally deliberately done something or invented something was immediately withdrawn because you accept what counsel says. So that's the basis on which I'm proceeding. I've just asked Mr. Demirdjian to do a check and he says there were 40 pages of questions about Brod during the course of examination-in-chief, so I think my couple of questions are pretty limited.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the gist of my objection was the fact that Ms. Korner was putting to the witness that he didn't mention this particular incident. I don't have a problem if she is exploring all this. She can ask the question, but the problem of putting that to the witness is not -- is not appropriate because it was Ms. Korner who was objecting for these line of questions. And if I had the opportunity, Your Honours, I would have -- I would have gone into the matter of who created the Muslim municipality of Bosanski Brod, the Croatian municipality of Bosanski Brod, the Serb municipality of Bosanski Brod, but it was -- it is not in our indictment, I agree, and it was the objection by Ms. Korner. Now, Ms. Korner is objecting, Your Honours accepted, I went very limited for the very limited purpose, like Your Honours said, because the Bosanski Brod was covered by the territory of the CSB Doboj. That is the only purpose, to show the situation in the territory of CSB Doboj prior to break-out of the hostilities. And, therefore, I wasn't in a position to put all the questions that I wanted to put or could have put to the witness. And now Ms. Korner is using that to state that the witness never mentioned it or testing his credibility on that. I don't think that's appropriate. That was the gist of my objection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I said I'll accept that Mr. Zecevic had have been allowed to continue in the face of my objections would have dealt with those matters, and I'm not -- I withdraw the suggestion that the witness deliberately avoided dealing with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we continue. Could the witness be escorted back to the stand.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, just to put a date to this, I think you have a note in your diary for the 24th of February, 1992, about a meeting that took place, in fact a major meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is one of the translations that came through yesterday but I just want to make one small point on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If you turn up your diary, please, 24th of February, 1992, in Derventa. There was a meeting, was there not, another one of these major meetings at which you attended, Mr. Delimustafic, Mr. Zepinic, Colonel Kolecevic [phoen] and others, do you see your note?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And there was a man called Radovanovic who was there, was there not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I am sorry, I must intervene again, Your Honours. If we can have the document on the monitor for the benefit of our clients. And for the benefit of the interpreters as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to put one small point and you've got the diary there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the accused don't, and I believe they are entitled to have before them what is referred to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. We'll see, I don't know whether we can find it. 20103 is the diary. It's page 174 of that document. There's a bit where he has noted Delimustafic speaking. Yes. Could we go to the next page, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah, we can see Mr. -- there's -- you can see the list of attendees.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do Your Honours want to have it up in English as well? I just want to put one small point. No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then Mr. Delimustafic speaking. Could you go, please, to the next -- we can see him at the bottom. Stay where you are. Mr. Radovanovic, who was he?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radovanovic was, if I remember correctly, well, yes, yes, president of the municipal board of SDS from Brod. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And he says: "Nobody wants to understand the Serbs in Bosanski Brod, no Serb can cross the bridge."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think you need to go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And does he say there somewhere or in your note: "The government of Bosnia-Herzegovina should reflect on how to protect the border. People have become so agitated they, themselves, have become an army. At the wish of these people, yesterday, Bosanski Brod was declared a municipality"? Is that a correct translation of what you've written?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm reading what Radovanovic said, but I haven't come to this point yet. Part of his remarks have to do with what I spoke of a moment ago, who had benefit from having the bridge closed down and who suffered because of it. I'm looking for it. Is it on the second page or third page?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did he -- can you see a part where he apparently, according to the English translation, said that yesterday the municipality had been declared?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'm looking for. That's what you said. It's after this, "The government of the BH should look into ...," right? Yes, yes, it's that paragraph, yes: "Yesterday, the municipality of Bosanski Brod was proclaimed according to the wishes of that people."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that was -- we are talking about, just so there's no misunderstanding, a Serb municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me read out the whole thing once again, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, don't, please, just tell us --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The revolt of the people is on the rise. They are going to become an army themselves. Yesterday, the municipality of Bosanski Brod was" -- I really don't know who this refers to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, this is the head of the SDS, isn't it? He is referring to a Serbian municipality being declared?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not what is written here. It doesn't say Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's try to look at the context once again, but it really does not say Serb. That is not what is written here. How to protect the border, revolt among the people is on the rise, they are going to turn into an army themselves, yesterday the municipality of Bosnia Brod was proclaimed according to the wishes of that people, I don't know who this refers to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You are not suggesting, are you, that it was a declaration of a Croat municipality of Bosanski Brod?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not trying to say that either. I'm just trying to decipher this. I mean, to place it into a context to be sure of what I'm saying. Because you see here at the beginning he says that none of the Serbs can cross the bridge in Brod, and then further on he says well possibly --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Stop, stop. Look at, please, your entry for the 10th of March, 1992, which is -- move it through the diary to the 10th of March.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 107B, 20103.02. Tab 107B. Okay. Can we go, please, to Radonovic [sic] again which is on the next page, please, in English. No, there's that's fine. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Item number 5: "In case legal authorities begin to function, the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Brod will be put on ice ..." Do you agree that's what you wrote?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wait a moment, are we talking about the 10th or the 24th now? A moment ago you took me back to the meeting of the 10th, what I wrote down then.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The 10th of -- no, I didn't. The 10th of March, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, the 10th of March, sorry, I went back to the 10th of February. I'm really sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You can look at it on the screen, Mr. Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Found it. The 10th of March, Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's just one simple question, Mr. Bjelosevic, don't go into anything else: Do you agree that clearly at that earlier meeting and this meeting, Mr. Radovanovic is talking about the establishment of a Serbian municipality in Bosanski Brod? That is the only question.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I would like to look at this in its entirety, in the entire context. I attended the meeting and I have to tell you that the municipality was full of uniformed people and --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Bjelosevic, I'm going to prevent you because, as you know, we say that is irrelevant. All that I'm trying to establish is that there was a Bosanski Brod Serbian municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, is this contested by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honours. I haven't the faintest idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Could the Defence let us know?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is precisely why I don't see what is the point. There is no contention that there existed throughout the Bosnia-Herzegovina the different municipalities, the Muslim municipality, the Croatian municipality and the Serb municipality, within the same territory of the previous municipality that existed in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So how much further do we need to --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we don't -- but -- I am sorry. I really -- all I'm asking is a simple, straightforward question which the witness at the moment is not particularly keen on answering. I made my objections about this. If the evidence had gone untested or unchallenged in the 40 pages of evidence this witness gave, you would never have known that there was a Serbian municipality of Bosanski Brod set up. Now, I don't want to take it any further, and, Your Honours, I didn't want to take it any further even with the diary, but I couldn't get the witness to agree with me, as you saw, and only Your Honours can decide this case on the evidence and not counsel's suggestions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I may have a constructive solution, perhaps, Your Honours. The Defence is ready to stipulate that this is the diary of Mr. Bjelosevic. We can stipulate. The diary talks for itself. It's written here what is written, and then the Prosecutors may rely on certain portions of this diary and the Defence may rely on the other portions of this diary, and, therefore, we can avoid all these questions about it, about the contents of the diary. We are ready to stipulate, this is his diary, we believe that the Office of the Prosecutor checked the contents of the diary, they had it -- they are taking it each and every day, they want to make a photocopy of it, so we believe that is -- and the witness confirms that its his diary, so we don't have to contest that. We are not contesting it. Therefore, we are ready to stipulate the diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Which stipulation you would accept, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We are talking about -- sorry, Your Honour, we are talking about two completely different things. I'm not interest in his diary entries on this matter. The only reason I referred to his diary entries was because I couldn't get him to admit that there was a Serbian municipality of Bosanski Brod declared at this particular date. And you can't just stipulates to the diary. The diary entries on their own may be meaningless and we can't interpret them unless we ask him about them. You can't just stipulate, of course we agree that's his diary, but the importance of the entries only relates to the evidence. Mr. Zecevic's suggestion is so wholly irrelevant on this particular point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Let's proceed in the manner we are going. We may find at the end of the day that that is a shorter course.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, no, no, I don't want to waste my valuable time on this, but we may have to have an argument. This diary in itself is utterly meaningless. It's his own notes, it's only when it's related to the events or he explains them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I heard you, Ms. Korner. I fully understand what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Right. Your Honours, I have, in fact, completed -- and can I say, it's quite clear, I would never have referred to this diary if he had simply answered the question directly, yes, there was such a declaration. Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we leave, please, Bosanski Brod, which is all I intend -- the two questions, or the only two questions that I intend to ask you, and just deal with the take-over of Doboj, the allegation you make that -- and you made in answer to the Judges, that the only armed people who were coming into Doboj back from the Croatian front were those who had joined the Croatian forces, is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that that is what I had said, that the only ones who were coming were Croats, as you had put it, no. What I was saying was that people were coming, people in uniform and with weapons, coming from the front and Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, what you actually said because you were specifically asked about this by one of the Judges --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can we have the reference, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just wait. That is exactly what I'm looking for. Right. 19443.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Judge Delvoie: "Mr. Zecevic, before we go to that one, Mr. Bjelosevic, you said that it would happen that members of all sorts of formations would come back from Croatia, the Croatian front, I suppose to their home areas in the Doboj area, they would come wearing uniforms and they would often carry weapons. They would come wearing uniforms and all different sorts of formations, you said. Am I correct by taking that generally the uniforms were JNA or would that be other uniforms as well? "A. Of course some wore JNA uniforms, those that belonged to JNA units. However, what I meant here was they were primarily members of the Croatian National Guards, the HOS units from Croatia and the other units that had been established there. People from the Doboj region went and joined these units as volunteers." Now, it may be that I misunderstood and if so I withdraw the suggestion that's what you said, in fact it wasn't just members of HOS, as you put it, who were coming back armed, it was also Serbs who had responded to the mobilisation for the war in Croatia, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did say other units as well, and on another occasion I said that of course Serbs responded to the JNA call-up and that there were those who were armed. And there's no denying that. They moved about and I don't know what your specific question is. I did not deny that there were Serbs who were uniformed, armed and who were in the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And by May of 1992 not only there were Serbs who had been in the JNA, but there were paramilitary organisations actually moving into the Doboj area, weren't there, Serb paramilitary organisations?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me try to answer this question as clearly as possible so that there's no confusion. As for paramilitary formations, I'm talking about paramilitary formations now, although we were talking about arming. In the second half of 1992, in the beginning of 1992, actually, all the way up until the beginning of May, as far as Doboj was concerned at least, Serbs responded to the JNA call-up. Please try to understand this very carefully now. In that period until May, to the best of my knowledge, there were not any Serb paramilitary formations in the area. When the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was proclaimed and when the JNA withdrew from the area, what happened was that certain units, smaller ones, started behaving outside the system, as it were, and they assumed the nature of paramilitary structures. I think that I had said that before as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm putting to you, let me put this quite clearly, and I'll give you the names, that the White Eagles, a group that are well known to you, turned up in Doboj before May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I am not familiar with that group. I really would want to see who these White Eagles were before the month of May. I really do not know about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: A group calling themselves Predo's wolves came into Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean Pedro's or Preda's wolves?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think I mean Predo's, but anyhow you know perfectly well who I'm talking about. They were there, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I was telling you a moment ago. It was a unit which was part of the JNA, so it's one of those units that were part of the JNA. They were mainly individuals from Ozren. However, in early May, as the JNA started to withdraw, the unit started operating quite autonomously and if they have wrestled themselves out of a system, then I suppose you could call them a paramilitary unit. And they weren't the only ones but they weren't the White Eagles.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What action -- sorry, and these people were terrorising, weren't they, the non-Serb population?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. According to my knowledge, they engaged in rogue behaviour in May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I am sorry. My specific question --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Criminal behaviour, interpreter's addition.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: My specific question was they were terrorising the non-Serb population, but you said yes to that even though you got the qualification.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, let me deal with some of the facts for the take-over. At the last session of the Doboj Municipal Assembly, Mr. Ninkovic, who was head of the SDS, proposed a division of the Doboj town, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had information to that effect. I don't know who proposed that, but that there was talk of Petar Uric street which divides the urban core of the town from Orasje and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The SDA members of the Assembly did not agree with that division and they left, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the details, I didn't attend the Municipal Assembly meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But you did know, didn't you, that there was no agreement that was arrived at at the Assembly about any division of Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My information at the time was that they were trying to reach an arrangement to divide the town by reference to that particular street. Where these discussions took them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Well, before the take-over on the night of the 2nd to the 3rd of May, there was no agreement reached. You knew that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that no final agreement was reached. However, to make it easier for you to understand, the fact of the matter was that just beyond that street it was the Muslim forces which held that part of town, whereas this other end of town, the urban core of the town, were under the control of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So, what are you calling the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were certain forces of theirs which held that part of town under their control. You have the reports that I sent on that issue. There were Green Berets and members of the Patriotic League, and some of it was from the Territorial Defence that was under their organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Weren't they just Muslim citizens who you were calling Green Berets, members of the Patriotic League? Weren't they just Muslims who happened to live in that part of the town?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were armed formations. You can see that in those documents. There were squads, platoons, companies. They had their commanding structures. They had military instructor come to train the forces over there, and now that we are discussing it, at Gradina itself, sometime in April, I can't remember the exact date, they hoisted a flag which caused quite a bit of anger and there were threats that the area would come under attack from the army. I went to see Mr. Alicic, the president of the Municipal Assembly at the time and he used his authority to calm the situation down. The flag was taken down and no major incident happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: What is this line of question because I think it's educated fact. All this events was covered by adjudicated fact. For example, adjudicated fact 1 to 66 cover all this split of Doboj and all this [indiscernible]. So what is the purpose of asking this question?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I read that to him deliberately, Mr. Krgovic, and the purpose of asking the questions is because, so far, every adjudicated fact that we have, this witness has challenged. So I'm trying to find out what he does accept. But thank you for the helpful intervention, Mr. Krgovic. I rather think the Judges had realised I was reading the adjudicated fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This was, wasn't it -- this was your excuse, your and the Serbs' excuse for taking over the town of Doboj, as you've already told us, the alleged attack that was about to happen an alleged attack?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't an alleged attack. That's how it was. It was just a matter of time and of who would keep the town under their control and there was information gathered at the time both by national security and public security, and I do believe that the information is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's deal with what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Ms. Korner, just one matter. The witness's answer on 71/25 was recorded as part of your question. There's no answer recorded of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: From the words, "That's how it was." Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What happened was this: The CSB was taken over and all non-Serb officers were -- police officers were expelled, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that they were expelled. How do you mean "expelled"?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thrown out of the police station.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, expelled and fled is not one in the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Some fled, many were arrested, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What followed next, the arrests around the town is not something that I took any part in or was specifically informed of, and I've already said as much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But, Mr. Bjelosevic, I understand that, but you were there for the take-over, your CSB could not have been taken over without your consent and knowledge, could it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between the 2nd and the 3rd, I was not in the police building. It was at around 8.00 or 7.30 in the morning on the 3rd that I arrived there. But I'm not denying what you are saying that there were people arrested, including members of the police. If that's what your question is about, then you are right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. That was the first part of my question. I need to go back then, please. You were involved, Mr. Bjelosevic, weren't you, in the planning of this take-over?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The whole take-over was planned without any reference to you or input by you, is that what you are telling the Court?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it had been planned and that an order had been issued for the engagement of the army on that particular task, and it was carried out on the night between the 2nd and the 3rd of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: By the army, and particularly in respect of the CSB by the police as well, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the buildings that were taken over at the time was the centre or the station. It comes down to the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Taken over by police officers with the assistance of the army?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that it was taken over by the army. The army. It was in the morning that the police took over the building. I was able to see that some offices in the building were forcibly entered. I don't think that police officers would have done that had they been there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But I just want to get this quite straight, Mr. Bjelosevic. You are saying, are you, that you knew what was going to happen but you stood back from it and took no part?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me be quite specific and clear. I was at the place from where the action started. Lipac on the slopes of Mount Ozren. I knew that the military action would go ahead. I stayed up there until the morning. I was up at Lipac until the morning. Once the action was carried out, I came to town to the police building.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Final question before we break: Who do you say was in charge of the police forces that is were involved in this take-over?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What the extent of the police forces participated in that was, I don't know, but there is a letter which I obtained at a later date which was also addressed to the command of the operational group and the Municipal Assembly. I handed it over here where the individuals who signed themselves as the defenders of Lipac say that Obren Petrovic had gathered them and was in command. You have that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah. So we are back to this, aren't we, everything that happened in Doboj for the next two months or so, the fault is that of Obren Petrovic? That's what you are saying, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not claiming that Obren is to blame for everything. The circumstances were the way they were. I only told you what I knew about it and what the letter said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just finish this, Your Honour, and then we'll --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Obren Petrovic was your inferior. You were his superior officer. We went through that. Are you telling this Court that of his own bat, without any input from you, he was in charge of the police that night?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I said. I only said what the letter said. I said where I was up until the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Did you -- Mr. Bjelosevic, did you put Mr. Petrovic in charge of the police that night?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No sort of authorisation was requested of me, nor did I give any, and I said at the beginning, according to the information I had, it was the army that took over the building. As far as I know, the police participated in the taking over of some other buildings in terms of providing security until the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again without any instructions or input from you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, allow me to make it quite clear, when the action was launched, the commander who was in charge of it and who ordered it, Major Stankovic, assessed the situation in the way that the police force should not be the one involved in the taking over of the police building of their own members. The police force engaged on that night was mixed. There were Serbs, Muslims, and Croats among them. I know that the arrangement was that these people should be treated fairly and that there should be no violence. There is no doubt that the town was taken over. This is not in dispute. I'm merely trying to explain through various details how it all played out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I would let everybody have their five minutes back so we'll reconvene at 2.35

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: --- Break taken at 1.50 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, just before we adjourned when you were explaining that you had nothing whatsoever to do with the take-over, the planning, or the execution thereof, you said at page 74, line 5: "What the extent of the police forces participating in that was, I don't know, but there is a letter which I obtained at later date addressed to the command of the operational group. I handed it over here with the individuals who signed themselves as the defenders of Lipac say that Obren Petrovic gathered them and was in command. You have that document." Now, this is a document you've not given certainly not to us before. Is this a document you'd given to the Defence before? You had given it to the Defence? Sorry, you have to say yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not to the Defence. When I went home, that was submitted with all the other copies. I didn't deny so categorically that I didn't know anything about that and that I was in no way involved. If I have to repeat, I can say that I knew that that would happen that evening. There's no doubt about that. And I sent this document with all the other copies of all the other documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's one of the documents you say which you gave to VWS. I may say I'm not interested in the contents but I want to ask you about the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We've only just had it translated, Your Honours, because it was only given to us at the beginning of the week. We've done the translation and it's on Sanction if that can be put ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that the document you referred to earlier this morning, or this afternoon, rather?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Where did you get the document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That document was sent to several addresses. You can see the list of the addressees at the bottom, and I received the document at the time when it was sent all those addresses, somebody gave it to me, but I don't remember who it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And when was that? There's no date on this document.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in the course of 1993, if my memory serves me properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The document is not signed?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, it was signed with the words combatants of the Lipovac company, that's how it was drafted. There were a lot of such letters with similar contents and I don't mean in terms of the facts but in terms of various demands, but there were no signatures. Those documents would be signed in general terms by combatants of this or other group or company.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Nothing to show where it was sent, any stamp, any receipt. Would not these people have stamped a receipt on it? Received on such and such a day, the operations group or the municipal board or the president of the Municipal Assembly or the president of the Executive Board? Wasn't that standard practice in 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember who gave it to me, and as for the list of the addresses to which it was sent you can see that, and I know that I already discussed this document with some people at that time. At that time the address -- the signatories of this document were mentioned. I don't know how relevant it is, but persons like Slobodan Devic and others were mentioned as being the authors of the documents. But let me go back to my service, that was the objective of this letter, that was its goal.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Of course you know what evidence Obren Petrovic gave, don't you, in this Court?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know some of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Did you watch him giving evidence?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read the summaries that are published by the SENSE agency at the end of the day so I know more or less what was said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's the last question I want to ask about this, the tenor of your evidence when asked questions by Mr. Zecevic is that effectively Petrovic was in charge and certainly during the months of May, June -- May and June? That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your evidence to this Court when asked questions by Mr. Zecevic has been to the effect that you were not there and Mr. Petrovic was in charge of the police activities in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, and if we are familiar with the structure of the police, the police would be in the public security station, not in the Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. That's all I want to ask. Thank you. Now, can we deal, please, with the events in Doboj. The Muslim population was ordered to surrender its weapons, wasn't it, in the town of Doboj during the take-over?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was an appeal. By a certain time in the afternoon on the 3rd of May, they were invited to surrender their weapons and not engage in any combat, in any armed conflicts. I don't know what the dead-line was, it may have been 1700 hours, but I am not sure. I know that about an hour and an hour and a half before that dead-line, strong fire was opened in the -- along the stretch parallel to the Petko Djuric street, as we have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that strong fire by the Muslims, is that what you are suggesting?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was on both sides that the fire was open and what ensued was an armed conflict. Up to then, there were no victims, no destruction, nothing. However, about an hour or an hour and a half before the expiry of that dead-line that was contained in the appeal to surrender weapons in order to avoid any armed conflicts, there was strong fire opened on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Isn't the truth that from the expiry of the dead-line, the JNA units, the army units shelled the Muslim districts of Doboj town, in particular a place called Kasija -- Carsija. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in town at the time. I was in the police building and first I heard fire being opened from infantry weapons and then I heard artillery explosions as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: During the course of the shelling, isn't it right that the mosque and the Roman Catholic church were badly damaged?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of that armed conflict, in the course of that combat, the Privedna Banka building was damaged and it caught fire, and I suppose there was damage inflicted on the other buildings that were close to that front line. As for the Catholic church, I can say that it is at the end of Petko Djuric street and one of the mosques, or, rather, two mosques are right above the Catholic church. I don't know how heavily damaged they were because I did not inspect the area at the time, I was not near the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: At the end of this shelling, large numbers -- the troops moved in and large numbers of Muslims were arrested and taken to prison; weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The combat lasted on until very late. It was already very dark when the shelling subdued. I don't know how late it was, I can't say at the moment, but there were no street lights so I don't know who moved around the town and what was going on. I stayed in the police building until very late that night and I could hear the shattering of the shop window glass. Then I called the police station and asked them to see what was going on. There was no more gun-fire but I could hear the sound of the breaking glass. A few police officers were sent out and it was established that some groups had broken shop windows on a goldsmith's shop and on a department store, I believe. The two were both very close to the police building and that's what I heard. I don't know what else was happening, it was dark, I did not move about the town so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You say that you heard artillery. The only people who had artillery that night were the Serb troops, weren't they, the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Smaller calibre cannons mortars had also been obtained by all the sides that were preparing for future conflicts, but the truth is that the JNA was best equipped, that it had the best artillery tools and armoured equipment. Whether fire was opened on both side or just one side, I don't know, but I know that immediately thereafter shells started falling, or rather, that it started happening in early May from Tesanj and other places, shells started falling on Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I move to some of the other areas. Vukovace [phoen] Civcije?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civcije. Let me help you. Civcije.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That was occupied by the Serb troops on the 4th of May after a surrender of weapons had been ordered?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when that happened. I don't know the date, but I know that a demand was issued for every place that was known to have weapons that it was requested that the weapons be surrendered. I don't know what exactly happened there. I only know what I heard subsequently. I don't know have any firsthand knowledge about what happened there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And after that, during the course of May and June, people from that village were arrested, taken to camps, and mistreated, weren't they? You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I subsequently heard about that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Houses in that village were blown up as was the mosque; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mosque was blown up. I don't know when, I don't know on what date. And fire was set to a number of houses. I know that houses were not destroyed, but some were set on fire, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What about Grapska, let's deal with that. On the 10th of May, there was an ultimatum, wasn't there, to hand over their weapons?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the date. Again, I don't want to confirm that that was on that a date, but there was a demand to surrender weapons. There were a lot of armed people there. I, myself, sometime in April passed through that village from the direction of Modrica. There was an accident so I took the regional road and to my huge astonishment as I was passing through the village, there was a machine-gun nest. In the centre of the village there was a shelter made of sand bags, and there was 53-millimetre machine-gun and there was a crew of several people. So, yes, they were armed, as you said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But the village was then shelled, wasn't it? I am sorry, I should -- this one I can be rather more specific. It was subjected to fire from tanks, anti-aircraft missile mortars, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm familiar with the weapons, and when you get something wrong I'm bothered. There's no anti-aircraft missile mortars there, anti-aircraft guns. I know there was a demand on Grapska to surrender weapons, and I know that demand was never complied with. There were some armed activities over there later and those are very fierce activities. I wasn't there, so I wouldn't be able to furnish you with any detail, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You do know the aftermath, don't you? People that were taken prisoner were killed, weren't they, by a man called Nikola Jorgic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nikola Jorgic, again I can't give you any detail, I don't know. However, during that period of time some ugly comments were heard about Jorgic's comport and conduct. Now that we've mentioned that, that was one of the reasons why I had a strong argument with the Petrovic Defence because that Jorgic turned up in the army and then he turned up in the police station as a member of the reserve police, he appeared with his group. And that's what I found from the very beginning, something that bothered me, something that I couldn't agree with. And when I spoke to the Defence about that, his Defence was that he had been issued with an order to welcome those units and volunteers as TO members, and I continued to assert that. There was no foundation for that pursuant to the Law on National Defence, Territorial Defence could be engaged in protecting public law and order, but this was not the case. This was an armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, I am not quite clear. It may be that something went wrong with the translation. You are recorded in English as saying: "... something that bothered me, something I couldn't agree with. And when I spoke to the Defence about that, his Defence, what he had been issued was with" --

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the Defence, Obren, Obren Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Okay. We'll come to Jorgic in a moment, but it's right also, wasn't it, that during the shelling, people were actually killed, during the shelling of Grapska?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably there were some casualties.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And after the army went in, they separated, didn't they, the women and children from the men and the men were taken to camps and also the prison in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that that is how it happened. I was not there and I don't know. And at the time I did not have any specific information on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm going to look at some of the information that was available to you at the time. Can I just finish with one other place. Sevarlije, was that shelled in mid-June?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sevarlije.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I agree, I have enormous difficult with words that have Cs and Js in it. But that's the one I'm talking about, was that shelled in mid-June?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when there was combat at that place. There was also an appeal to surrender weapons there as well, as far as I know, and there were some combat there, some fighting going on, but what happened to those weapons, whether it was taken or surrendered or not at all, I don't know what was the outcome. But I know that something was going on there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So in each of these cases, you are saying that the shelling and firing on these villages was justified because, as you understand it because you say you weren't there, people were fighting, that the villagers were fighting? Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I never mentioned what was justified or unjustified or whether the force was proportional. What I know is that there was fighting there. I never justified any burning, any setting on fire, and I don't know how it came to be, whether it was through the action of weaponry or whether things were set on fire. What I do know is that in some villages there was combat, what I don't know are the details.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we have a look, please, then there's a few reports that you say you would -- you had intelligence. Let's see if you knew about these. Can we look, first of all, please, at -- no, we can't. 16B, please, which is document 20122. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is a report signed "Milos" dated the 12th of May: "According to insufficiently verified reports, an artillery attack on the Muslim village of Grapska, Doboj municipality, caused very many civilian casualties, including children. The Serbian defence forces were forced to carry out the attack since there were strong Green Berets forces in the village which were firing on villages inhabited by Serbs." Were you aware of this kind of intelligence?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I haven't received this information and I never used to receive information directly from the operatives who gathered information in the field. I would get compilations and mostly the information relating to the enemy forces and then I compared that with the information collected by the military intelligence and that way when we combined the two, we were able to improve the quality of our intelligence. But trust me, I never requested any of the operatives to tell me anything, nor did I know their operative names.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But did you get -- whether you saw or received this one in particular, did you hear that there were -- through your intelligence, very many civilian casualties, including children?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was later, after the events when I heard that there were casualties. I don't know their number, I don't know how many civilians, how many members of armed formations, and I don't know whether there were any children, and if so, how many. I really know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we look, please, at a report of the following day, which is document, please, 20004. Tab 17:

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: "According to the latest reports," says Milos, "there is no imminent danger of a direct attack on Doboj by units of HOS and the Muslim armed force, although the security situation is still difficult since units of the JNA and SOS do not control large parts of the Doboj municipality, primarily those inhabited by Croats and Muslims." Who was SOS?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. The author of this report ought to know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you agree that on the 13th of May, there was no imminent danger of a direct attack on Doboj by units of HOS or the Muslims, the Patriotic League, the Green Berets, whatever you call them?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time there was a concentration of forces in the north, that is from the direction of Derventa. At Kotorsko and in Johovac. There were parts of the Croatian Army brigades there, the 64th Rijeka Brigade, there are documents about that, then one brigade from Osijek, from Slavonska Pozega, and I think also parts of the brigade from Slavonski Brod. And we observed that area constantly. We were on alert because you have to understand, it used to be one state, the service was very well developed, it used to have great network of informers and we used to receive good intelligence both from Croatia and from the areas controlled by Muslim forces. An option to attack along the national road was seriously considered; that is coming from north, from Johovac, in order to connect with Tesanj and in that way to control the Bosna river valley.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The short answer is no you don't agree with that assertion that there's no imminent danger on May 13th?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't know about the specific day, it's very difficult for me to speak about specific days from where I sit now. I mean, it's been quite awhile ago, but there was definitely a possibility of an attack coming from the north and the possibility of those forces linking up with the forces along the Bosna river. We permanently followed the situation and that problem was definitely very much present at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we look finally on this part of the events at document, please, which is already an exhibit, P1337.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, tab number?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Tab 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, this is by the same author, Milos, and the report is dated the 17th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Perhaps we ought to go to the second page so you can just confirm that. Sorry, can we go to the next page, please, in both the B/C/S and in English. Yes. Okay, let's go back, please, back to the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The report begins that: "In the Doboj region, the Serbian Territorial Defence in co-operation with police units have started offensive operations against the armed formations of HOS and the Green Berets." Pause there. Do you agree that is a correct summary of the situation?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 17th of May?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about which direction this man speaks. I can see that he mentions Doboj, Brod, and Derventa, but it doesn't quite agree with the date and also the Territorial Defence because on the 12th and the 13th of May, the VRS had already been established, so maybe, I don't know. Listen, it's hard for me to remember things by days. I also know that sometime in May, I don't know exactly on which date, I went to Belgrade. I took off from the Banja Luka airport. But let me tell you, in this northern part, there were constant skirmishes, or to put it militarily, the front was continuously active. There was fire contact all the time. Well, I suppose that both sides were testing the forces on the other side and I assume that there was some combat as this man wrote.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I actually only want to deal with two small parts of this. In the middle of the first paragraph, the author says: "Many flats in Doboj were searched, many Muslim and Croatian citizens were arrested." Is that, to your knowledge, a correct assertion?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, later on I saw in the files that there was a number of detained persons. How, on what basis, and who was detained, that is something that I cannot comment on, because at the time I didn't know what was going on in relation to this because the security work was performed by the station. But probably, or not even probably, definitely, yes, people were detained in large numbers. That is what I saw from documents later on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We'll come on to the prison log-book in a moment. It goes on to say: "During searches and arrests, there was incorrect behaviour by so-called Special Forces of the Serbian armed formations. Apart from visible injuries suffered by the arrested persons, there was appropriation of private property by those carrying out the searches. Such behaviour met with the indignation and condemnation of all honest citizens especially the mobilised Serbian TO who threatened to use arms against the Special Forces from Banja Luka and the Special Forces organised by a man called Bozovic." Firstly, who are the special forces from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We already discussed this during examination-in-chief, and that is when I told the Chamber what I know about how many people from Banja Luka came and what was their status. And I'm going to repeat it once again. I'm not aware of any special unit from Banja Luka as a separate formation that acted independently, except a number of people who performed security for the inspectors who arrived in order to help the work of the national security. That's all I know about people from Banja Luka. I really know nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. Pause there, we'll go on to the next one. So, you know nothing about any so-called Special Police under the leadership of a man called Ljuban Ecim or Samardzija, first name also?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That they were there as a unit and acted as a unit in the area of Doboj? No. Apart from the people I've already mentioned who had that particular status, and as far as I know they didn't arrive all at once. They had shifts, exchanging shifts. So people who came first went back and then the following team came and I think it was about 15 or 16 people in total. Or maybe in two shifts or in three shifts, I wouldn't know the details, but I think that the number is about 15 or 16 of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Secondly, the man called -- Special Forces organised by a man called Bozovic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the presence of Bozovic and the forces ascribed to him, as far as I know, there was 10 to 12 people. I think that Bozovic was a major, and again, I have to emphasise that I do not know the truth but I can tell you what I heard.
